svg.data-optics-qsfp28: datasheet: each 100G QSFP28 port takes 1 x 100 GbE or breaks out to 2 x 50G, 4 x 25G or 4 x 10G. The datasheet's transceiver list names the modules and cables it is qualified with; more are referred to the vendor's site.

Two drawings landing within 0.2% of a round 10.0 is the same evidence that settled edgecore/exp800-16o's width, and it settles this one: 442 is the number the art was drawn to. THE PHOTOGRAPH'S INK BOX IS NOT ITS FACE, and this is the second device in a row where that mattered. Its ink spans 104 rows, which at 960 px / 442 mm is 47.9 mm - taller than a 1RU. Rows 296-301 are a flat band of uniform grey, 102.3 to 102.4, whose colour saturation climbs from 2.9 to 5.8 while the panel below varies from 62 to 138: the chassis LID, the shot being very slightly from above. The rear photograph has the same band at the same rows. Excluding it the face is about 95 px = 43.7 mm against the stated 43.94. NO TAPER: the ink spans 960 px at every height on both faces. THE ELEVATIONS ARE STRETCHED VERTICALLY, as the EXP800's front was. The front reads 486 px tall where 43.94 mm at 10.0045 would be 439.6, so its y scale is 486 / 43.94 = 11.0605 and every front y below is read on that second scale."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"863 W MAXIMUM, FROM THE VENDOR'S PRODUCT PAGE, and the datasheet states no consumption figure at all - the same situation as the EXP800 and the same number. THE STAGED PHOTOGRAPHS ARE THE VENDOR'S OWN, BYTE FOR BYTE. All four images the product page serves - EXP100-32X-FF, -B, -F and -A under wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ - were fetched and their SHA-256 digests compared against the staged copies. The page also states a maximum draw of 863 W, which the datasheet does not."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 16 QSFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-31/port-32)."},"the-front-does-not-carry-over":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AND THE ISSUE'S OWN ADVICE SAID IT WOULD. roc-ops/Portrayal#321 recommends building edgecore/exp800-16o first and carrying it over as "the only route that gets these two a measured panel". THAT IS RIGHT FOR THE REAR AND WRONG FOR THE FRONT. Thirty-two ports need 353 mm of wall where sixteen need 251, so this device's wall opens at 45.30 mm where the EXP800's opens at 98.16 - and everything to its left is compressed into a third of the room. The console bezel measures x 9.75 to 24.24 here against the EXP800's 57.97 to 74.77. Not one feature of the left cluster is in the same place. THE 1PPS JACK IS THE CHECK ON THE TWO SOURCES. Its gold nut segments at x 29.69-36.18, y 22.87-28.12 on the elevation and x 30.39-36.37, y 23.02-28.09 on the photograph - 0.7 mm apart on a feature 6 mm across, read at 10.0 and 2.17 px/mm. That agreement is what licenses the rest of the left-hand measurements."},"the-management-stack":{"confidence":"measured","note":"ONE HOUSING, TWO CONNECTORS, as on edgecore/exp800-16o and edgecore/dcs511. The bright bezel at the right of the port row reads x 410.8 to 427.5 and y 10.4 to 32.1 - a 1000BASE-T RJ-45 over a USB 3.0 in one moulding. The datasheet lists them separately, "1 x RJ-45 1G BASE-T management" and a "USB3.0 storage port" in its callout table, and the panel prints MGMT and USB above the stack. There is no stacked RJ45/USB part in this library, so the housing is drawn as a decor under both. THE CONSOLE IS SEPARATE AND AT THE FAR LEFT, bezel x 9.75-24.24 by y 17.63-32.33 against std/rj45@2's 15.8 by 13.2, with CONSOLE printed beneath it. One console, as on the EXP800 and unlike the DCS240 and DCS511 which carry two."},"the-optical-wall":{"confidence":"measured","note":"EIGHT BLOCKS OF FOUR, AND TWO SOURCES AGREE ON EVERY BLOCK TO 0.4 MM. The bright perforated band that separates the two cage rows runs the length of each block and segments cleanly in both the datasheet elevation at 10.0045 px/mm and the photograph at 2.1719 - a factor of 4.6 apart in resolution.

Least squares on each gives a block pitch of 44.739 and 44.666; the block width reads 38.72 and 38.68. With std/qsfp-ganged@1's registry pitch of 19.0 that is GANG 2 WITH A 6.70 GUTTER, and the first aperture opens at 45.30. AUTOCORRELATION DISAGREED AND WAS WRONG, which is worth recording. The dominant period over the cage band reads 43.78 mm on the elevation and 43.74 on the photograph - both about a millimetre under the edge fits. The wall's inter-block gaps are not uniform (the steps read 44.2, 46.9, 44.2, 43.5, 43.7, 46.5, 44.2 on the photograph and the same pattern on the elevation), and a periodic fit to an irregular comb lands below the mean spacing. THE EDGES ARE MEASURED IN TWO PLACES AND THE PERIOD IS INFERRED FROM ONE; the edges win. ROWS are the weaker axis. The elevation puts the upper opening at 3.80 to 13.83 mm and the lower at 22.33 to 32.64, a row pitch of 18.54; the photograph gives about 4.4 to 12.6 and 22.6 to 30.7, a pitch of 18.2. The two row tops agree within 0.6 mm and the pitches within 0.35, so 4.10 and 18.40 are used. The drawn opening heights, 10.04 and 8.15 against std/qsfp-ganged@1's 9.58, bracket the registry figure rather than agreeing with it, which is why the part's own height is drawn and not theirs."},"the-rear-is-the-exp800s":{"confidence":"measured","note":"PROVEN AGAINST THIS DEVICE'S OWN ELEVATION, NOT ASSUMED. The rear drawing on datasheet page 2 renders at 9.9819 px/mm and carries the same furniture: PS1 at the LEFT, six fan trays numbered 6 to 1, PS2 at the right, red pull bars, red release latches at each supply's left edge. THE NUMBERS AGREE WHERE THEY MATTER. Colour-segmenting the six pull bars puts their centres on a 49.263 mm pitch with residuals of 0.34 mm or less, against the EXP800's 48.921 - 0.34 apart. The full-height seams either side of the fan block put PS1's right edge at 67.82 and PS2's left at 426.47, against the EXP800's 66.6 and 425.9 - within 1.2 mm on a 442 mm face. So edgecore/exp800-fan@1 and edgecore/exp800-psu-ac@1 are seated here rather than new parts being cut. The bay wall uses THIS device's own measurements - bar centre 97.24 and pitch 49.263 - not the EXP800's, because they are the better reading of this rear."},"the-system-lamps":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"FIVE LAMPS IN A 3+2 GRID, AND THIS IS THE WEAKEST THING IN THE MODEL. The datasheet's LED line names them - "System LEDs: Diagnostic, Locator, PSU, and Fan Status" - and the marks on the elevation fall in exactly the pattern the EXP800's enlargement resolves: three in the left column, two in the right. THE ONLY ELEVATION HAS CALLOUT ARROWS DRAWN THROUGH THE CLUSTER. Two of the nine leader arrows land on and beside it, and at this size a 2 mm lamp and a four-character legend are both about 3.4 mm wide, so which marks are windows and which are words cannot be told apart from the drawing alone. WHAT IS USED, AND WHY. The marks read x 27.74-31.24 and 36.23-39.48, rows y 13.79-15.14, 16.73-18.09 and 20.12-21.48. They are taken as the LAMPS, giving column centres 8.4 mm apart - against the EXP800's measured 8.2 mm on the same cluster in the same family. That agreement is the reason for the choice and not a proof of it; the legends are then placed outside the columns, where there is room for them and where the EXP800 prints its own. confidence is `drawing` rather than `measured` deliberately. g.data-description: the 1PPS timing input - a single coaxial jack beside the system lamps. THE DATASHEET CALLS IT AN SMA; the drawings put it at about 6 mm, which is SMB scale, and common/smb-jack@1 is seated on that basis. It states no group media because coax is not a pluggable cage and L40's optics question does not apply to it.
g.title: pps-in
